metadata.technology_specification: Man-Portable Thermal Imaging Sight (Infrared Thermal Scope)
metadata.technology_reasoning: Man-portable thermal imaging sights are typically infrared thermal scopes that detect thermal radiation to produce images in low visibility conditions. These devices dominate the market due to their portability, battery operation, and widespread use in military and law enforcement, with core technology based on uncooled microbolometer sensors, which are the industry standard for compact thermal imaging.

components.reasoning: This is the core detecting element that senses infrared radiation, universally present in all thermal imaging sights.
The optics focus IR radiation onto the sensor and provide the user interface for viewing; typically a separate, precision component.
Processes raw sensor data into a visible image; this electronic subsystem is standard and procured separately.
Essential for visual output of processed thermal images, always present as a distinct component.
Supplies power, typically a rechargeable battery pack designed for portability and field use.

components.component: User Interface Controls and Housing Buttons
components.reasoning: Controls for operating the device including brightness, zoom, and power, usually part of the external assembly but often modular enough to be considered a component.
Rugged enclosure providing mechanical protection and environmental sealing, typically a separate manufactured assembly.
Many modern units include onboard image recording and storage as a modular add-on, but it may not be present in all designs.

components.component: Mounting Interface (Rail Mount or Picatinny Mount)
components.reasoning: Facilitates attachment to weapons or other platforms; standard separate mechanical component in man-portable designs.
